title: LRU Cache
hints: You need three O(1) operations: find an entry by key, move an entry to the most-recent position, and remove the least-recent entry. A dict gives you the first; a list gives neither of the other two in O(1).
A doubly linked list ordered by recency supports unlink and insert-at-front in O(1) once you hold the node, and the dict maps key -> node. Sentinel head and tail nodes remove every edge case.

get: if present, unlink the node and reinsert it at the front, return its value. put: if present, update the value and move to front; otherwise create a node at the front and, if over capacity, unlink the node before the tail and delete its key from the dict.
